QUOTE: Nvidia has now sharpened “this fall” into a firmer target, confirming RTX Spark systems are scheduled to ship in October 2026 from six launch partners: Asus, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft Surface, and MSI.
SURROUNDING PASSAGE: Nvidia’s own DGX Spark desktop, which shares the same 128GB memory ceiling and 1-petaflop rating, was marketed at launch as capable of running models up to 200 billion parameters. Why RTX Spark’s local-model claim lands lower than its desktop sibling isn’t explained in Nvidia’s public materials, and it could come down to differences in how Windows manages memory versus the Linux-based DGX OS, or simply more conservative marketing math the second time around. Either way, nobody outside Nvidia has independently benchmarked RTX Spark yet, so both numbers should be treated as vendor claims until third-party reviewers publish results this fall.
Release Date, Launch Partners, and Pricing
Nvidia has now sharpened “this fall” into a firmer target, confirming RTX Spark systems are scheduled to ship in October 2026 from six launch partners: Asus, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft Surface, and MSI. Acer and Gigabyte are expected to add models after launch. No official USD pricing has been announced for any configuration, and as of September 2026 that’s still the case — Nvidia has narrowed the ship window but still hasn’t published pricing for any tier. HotHardware’s reporting describes four distinct silicon tiers rather than a single chip, which suggests Nvidia and its partners plan to spread RTX Spark across multiple price points rather than launch a single flagship SKU.
